Parking the whole roadmap. Under the Parking rule, the two items left in the roadmap become backlog entries:

- **Stage 2** (closure notices) becomes one deferred item.
- **Each of the three Track A Ranked-list items** (O2, O3, O4) becomes one deferred item.

The roadmap then moves to `specs/completed/` with a PARKED mark. There are no methodology or critique files to retire with it, because this roadmap came from your own words, not a spec.

I have no tools this turn, so here are the calls I'll run.

**1. Read the item schema and the existing backlog**

```
Glob  ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/*deferred*
Read  <that file>                      # Deferred-item schema
Read  specs/deferred_items.md          # may not exist yet
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`**

I'll add one dated section. The wording below is a draft and will be fitted to the schema's exact fields once I've read it.

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure email notices for boat operators (lock-closures O5, Track B, parked Stage 2)
      Boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing. Poll the closure log's live feed about every 10 minutes.
      Text-message notices are out of scope.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll each 10 minutes).
      Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (lock-closures O2, Track A, Ranked 1)
      Apply the Stage 1 closure-vs-gauge-level curve to the river-level forecast.
      Stage 1 found a closure chance below 2% under 3.1 m, rising to about 60% at 3.8 m (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md; plan 4).
      Size: small; one model run a day. Stage 1's single fit took 22 min on a laptop.
      Done when: each lock has a 7-day closure-risk outlook computed from the river-level forecast.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled across all 14 locks (lock-closures O3, Track A, Ranked 2)
      Stage 1 fit one curve. The four locks with the longest records show close to the same curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md).
      Size: about 14× Stage 1's data (Stage 1 used 1.8 GB over 11 years of daily gauge readings).
      Done when: there is a separate closure curve for each of the 14 locks, fit with pooling across locks.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (lock-closures O4, Track A, Ranked 3)
      A static map page of each lock's closure history.
      Size: about a day of work.
      Done when: boat operators can open a map showing the closure history of each lock.
```

**3. Retire the roadmap**

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit   specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
       # add under the title: PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (funding ended): 1 of 2 stages complete; remaining stage and Track A list to deferred_items"
```

The Stage 1 findings file and plan 4 stay where they are. The deferred items cite both.

Once these run, I'll confirm the commit and the final entries. The roadmap is then closed. Any of these items can come back later through the normal deferred-backlog process.
